body:
## Summary

This PR changes building pathfinding from eagerly expanding an entire map-sized field to **computing only the distances gameplay requests**, retaining the search frontier for later queries. It also makes field initialization cheaper and keeps partial fields behind resolving query APIs. This is the standard behavior in all game entry points, with no experimental mode switches.

The primary performance study measured **2.2–8.3% less total game CPU versus the master baseline**, before the additional initialization optimization. That optimization separately saved another **0.5–1.7% of total CPU** on four workloads. These are separate measurements, not a directly measured cumulative percentage for the final head; details and comparison boundaries are below.

## Complete change versus master

- **Demand-driven building fields.** Master finishes propagation when a field is rebuilt. This PR initializes the field, then extends a retained bucket queue only far enough to answer each request. It completes whole distance layers so equal-distance movement choices remain identical. Building and flag fields use this path automatically.
- **Cheaper initialization.** Ordinary buildings classify and write each cell once, replacing the initial full-field fill followed by a general flag-aware classification pass. Flags retain their special goal and obstacle rules. Initialization and seed scanning still cover the map; propagation is the work deferred by queries.
- **A clear query boundary.** Distance and movement APIs settle their inputs internally. The public full-array getter still returns a complete field. Preparation owns allocation, refresh and use timestamps; resolving a prepared field only extends its search. Callers do not need to coordinate partial reads.
- **One propagation kernel.** Resumable building searches and full-field resource/round-trip searches share the same expansion kernel. The existing round-trip system is preserved: constructing a round-trip field completes its parent, while reading a cached round-trip field does not force the parent to finish again.
- **Preserved cache and save behavior.** Obstacle/goal inputs and weighted water costs are frozen at rebuild time. Refresh deadlines, stuck-unit retries and idle eviction retain their existing policy. Saving, full-field consumers, forbidden-area escape and debug rendering complete fields where required. Saves retain their existing full-field representation; loaded fields start complete. Search queues follow their owning fields and are never serialized.
- **Regression coverage and documentation.** Tests cover the independent shortest-path oracle, all seven swim classes, paused terrain snapshots, query ordering, equal-cost movement, disconnected/capped distances, toroidal maps, frontier reuse and the public query boundary. The default gameplay query is tested to leave a paused frontier. Normal CI runs exercise this behavior without duplicate switched runs.

No save/replay/network format or version changes, new cache invalidation scheme, or intended gameplay/pacing changes. Benchmark instrumentation and temporary evidence are outside the implementation diff.

## Performance versus master

The [162-run controlled study](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/e6194e49895063a2d254e054a50d61dd2bed97cc/timing-study) compares the original master baseline **`1c49596f5`** with lazy implementation **`d50968d06`**, including integration overhead. These are net process-CPU reductions against master, not merely comparisons between two PR modes:

| Workload | Total CPU reduction versus master | Paired 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arena 128², 2 players | **4.31%** | 4.04–4.58% |
| Arena 256², 2 players | **2.48%** | 2.34–2.62% |
| Arena 512², 4 players | **8.25%** | 7.52–8.98% |
| Lakes 256², 4 players | **8.12%** | 7.91–8.33% |
| Arena 256², additional seed, 4 players | **2.25%** | 2.05–2.44% |
| Lakes 256², additional seed, 4 players | **3.55%** | 3.15–3.95% |
| Lakes 256², four synchronous checkpoints | **7.73%** | 7.49–7.97% |

The study used 54 matched blocks, six or twelve repetitions per variant/workload, alternating all variant orders. Building-gradient elapsed-time scopes fell **30–39% versus the study's eager PR mode**. Workloads differ substantially, so there is no single representative aggregate percentage. These are macOS release/headless measurements; intervals describe repeatability of the retained workloads, not all games or platforms.

The final implementation also includes the resolving-API cleanup, single-pass initialization and removal of the experimental switches. [API cleanup measurements](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/edf80b22276a345167bbc837b0d38fef9b11d1db/api-profile) did not establish an additional overall CPU gain or loss. The [initialization study](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/9c56176c6d8a504811cbf22468dde24940fc01a3/field-initialization) measured another **1.69%, 0.53%, 1.42% and 1.52%** less total CPU on the original 128² arena, 256² arena, 512² arena and lakes workloads respectively, comparing already-lazy implementations. Its 16 separate diagnostic runs found **31–36% less ordinary-building initialization time**. This supports an additional benefit beyond the main table, but a fresh final-head-versus-master study has not been run; the percentages should not be added or presented as a measured combined result.

## Costs and compatibility

Retaining frontiers and water snapshots trades memory for less propagation work. The controlled study measured approximately **0.3–5.5 MiB additional peak RSS versus master**, depending on workload. Completing pending fields shifts some work into saving: synchronous serialization cost about **12.6 ms more per save** than the study's eager PR mode (95% interval 3.4–21.8 ms). The checkpoint workload still reduced total CPU by 7.73% versus master. GUI asynchronous autosave latency and interactive frame-time distributions remain unmeasured.

The [final default-path validation](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/e226db74c9899693c41cb325e3f63a29d48399de/final-default) covers head **`c0c24b582`**: native macOS release build and five regression harnesses pass. Four full games (**65,442 ticks**) match the original baseline's per-tick checksums and initial/final save bytes, with no mode switches. A **1,024-tick continuation of an original save** also matches checksums and final save bytes. The initialization study additionally compared every initialized cell against the previous initializer on every rebuild across these games.

The linked evidence retains source commits, commands, seeds, hashes, raw timings, logs, checksum sidecars and save artifacts. [Original compatibility evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/ecc77866349e3f48ebad5712dff44eeeb08546d3) includes the pre-existing Maxima save-diagnostic caveat; this PR does not fix that unrelated issue.

Additional [cross-platform verification](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/ea8cc407df0ea92bbc4c701478d65ba4bdda9f2e/cross-platform) compares the original master and final head on macOS arm64 (Apple Clang), therig Linux x86_64 (GCC 15.2), and devlaptop Linux x86_64 (GCC 13.3). Two additional 8,192-tick four-AI games and a 4,096-tick continuation of the exact same master checkpoint produce **identical per-tick checksums on every host and between both implementations**: 9 paired comparisons, 61,440 compared tick pairs. All fresh-game checkpoint/final saves match across platforms. Linux gradient oracles also pass.

Save comparisons retain three pre-existing caveats rather than masking them: initial Echo alliance/vision fields are uninitialized before the first tick; Echo area-coordinate loading uses compiler-dependent argument evaluation order, producing swapped stored coordinates in both master and PR; and one devlaptop continuation differs only in the known out-of-bounds Maxima diagnostic sample plus the save hash. A repeated unchanged master run also changes that diagnostic value. Raw saves, exact comparisons and a telemetry parser are attached. The Echo coordinate issue is a real existing portability concern; matching checksums in these runs does not establish that it can never affect later gameplay. No gradient-induced simulation divergence was observed, but universal cross-platform save-byte identity is **not** claimed.

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36456275043) passes, including an identical 1,500-tick fixture trace across Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04, Windows and WebAssembly, also compared against macOS master and final head. Windows/WebAssembly coverage here is that fixture, not the longer AI workloads. Interactive play remains unverified; maintainer playtesting remains part of review.



The pre-existing Echo/Maxima issues uncovered above are addressed separately in [PR #383](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/pull/383). Its corrected builds match every saved file across macOS and both Linux hosts, with all 61,440 master-versus-fixed tick pairs unchanged in the tested workloads. The companion PR retains its own evidence and calls out the intentional correction to older GCC save-loading behavior.
title: Compute building gradients on demand
